There are a lot of leftovers in the fridge.
We do not have any bread.
How much food should I bring?
How many people are coming?
Are you coming on Saturday? It is at my place, from one.
I would like to. Is it a cookout or a potluck?
A potluck. Good question, most people never ask.
Then how many people are coming, and how much food should I bring?
About fifteen. One large portion is enough, nobody finishes anything anyway.
Is there anything you do not have yet?
We do not have any salad, and we already have too much dessert.
A salad, then. Homemade, or is it fine from the grocery store?
Nobody says it out loud, but homemade always wins.
Understood. And what happens to what is left?
Everybody takes the leftovers home. Bring a box.
Is it a cookout or a potluck?

Hi Thiago, it is Linda. About Saturday: it is a potluck, not a cookout, so everybody brings something. There are about fifteen of us, and we do not have any dessert yet, so do not bring one, we already have too much sugar in this office. If you want to make something homemade, bring a salad, because there are never enough of those. Do not worry about the amount: whatever is left, people take the leftovers home. See you at one.

Welcome to the store guide. If this is your first time with us, here is how it works. Fresh food is on your right and the frozen aisles are at the back. There are a lot of offers this week on fruit and vegetables, and there is not much left of the bread by six in the evening, so come early for that. Snacks are in aisle four, and yes, it is a whole aisle. If you cannot find something, ask any member of staff. We are open until eleven every day.

First, Linda calls Thiago and explains that Saturday is a potluck. Then he asks how many people are coming and how much food he should bring. After that, he goes to the grocery store and buys what is missing. Next, he makes a homemade salad, because there are never enough of those. Finally, everybody takes the leftovers home in a box.
